title: Which tops and bottoms can we shorten first?
description: Fourteen fifteenths is multiplied by twenty five forty seconds. Two pairs of numbers on the board are shortened, one after the other, before the multiplying starts. Keeko raises the doubt of stopping after the first pair.
teaching_notes: One idea: check every top against every bottom, and cancel each pair that shares a factor before multiplying. Watch for students who cancel one pair and stop, leaving an answer that is not in lowest form.

source: Multiply 14/15 × 25/42 and give the product in its lowest fo
video_script.why: A learner sees that more than one pair can be cancelled, and that every top and bottom pair must be checked.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own second example, fourteen fifteenths and twenty five forty seconds
video_script.anchor: the product of fourteen fifteenths and twenty five forty seconds, written as one fraction
video_script.wrong_move: cancels fourteen and forty two, then multiplies without checking the other pair
video_script.payoff_line: Fourteen fifteenths times twenty five forty seconds is five ninths
video_script.fraction_reading: fourteen fifteenths, twenty five forty seconds, five ninths, twenty five forty fifths
maths_rules: the slip: (1 × 25)/(15 × 3) = 25/45, which is 5/9 only after dividing by 5 again
video_script.design: One product of two fractions written as one fraction. Each pair that is shortened gets its own colour; the numbers left are plain.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the two fractions 14/15 and 25/42 with a times sign between them

marks.pose: the two fractions arrive with a times sign between them
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the product

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about multiplying two fractions.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Multiply fourteen fifteenths by twenty five forty seconds, and write the product in its lowest form.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the product in its lowest form?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the product as (14 × 25)/(15 × 42), unworked; the word cancelling appears with a pair of numbers linked by a line

marks.rule: the tops and the bottoms are outlined
marks.name: the word cancelling is written beside a linked pair
marks.all: every top is linked to every bottom in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Before multiplying fractions, look for a top and a bottom with a common factor.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Dividing that top and that bottom by the common factor is called cancelling.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Every top has to be checked against every bottom, one pair at a time.

marks.given: the two fractions are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fractions are fourteen fifteenths and twenty five forty seconds.

marks.find: the words To find and the product are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find their product in its lowest form.

marks.write: the product is written with the tops together over the bottoms together
marks.pairs: the tops 14 and 25 and the bottoms 15 and 42 are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write the product as fourteen times twenty five over fifteen times forty two.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>The tops are fourteen and twenty five. The bottoms are fifteen and forty two.

beats.on_screen: cancelling 14 and 42 by 14: 14 becomes 1 and 42 becomes 3; the working shows (1 × 25)/(15 × 3)

marks.first: the fourteen and the forty two are linked by a line
marks.res1: the one and the three replace them

beats.colours: the first pair in the accent colour
beats.moves_through: the 14 and the 42 change into 1 and 3
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, fourteen and forty two share the factor fourteen, so divide both by fourteen.
<bookmark mark='res1'/>The fourteen becomes one, and the forty two becomes three.

beats.on_screen: cancelling 25 and 15 by 5: 25 becomes 5 and 15 becomes 3; the working shows (1 × 5)/(3 × 3)

marks.second: the twenty five and the fifteen are linked by a line
marks.res2: the five and the three replace them

beats.colours: the second pair in a second colour
beats.moves_through: the 25 and the 15 change into 5 and 3
narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step three, twenty five and fifteen share the factor five, so divide both by five.
<bookmark mark='res2'/>The twenty five becomes five, and the fifteen becomes three.

marks.mult: the tops and the bottoms are multiplied
marks.low: a tick checks that the top and the bottom share no factor

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step four, multiply what is left, one times five on top and three times three below.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Five and nine share no factor, so the answer is in lowest form.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Fourteen fifteenths times twenty five forty seconds is five ninths.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: (1 × 25)/(15 × 3) = 25/45 appears with the pair 25 and 15 untouched; a tick for lowest form is crossed out; then 25 and 45 are shown sharing the factor 5

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows only the first pair shortened
marks.slip: a cross appears on the tick for lowest form
marks.fix: the twenty five and the forty five are linked by a line

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we shorten fourteen and forty two, and stop there.
Keeko gets a product of twenty five forty fifths.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>That has the right value, but it is not in lowest form.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Twenty five and forty five still share a common factor, which is five.
Every top must be checked against every bottom before we multiply.
